THE_ARCHITECT.talk.BELLKEEPER-BELLKEEPER: Look. I brought the bell back.
It is the last bell from the belfry at the foot of the Spire. It bears your maker's mark. Do you not recognize it?
I have cast ten thousand gears, beams, and bronzes. I do not keep ledgers for rubble. Since you hauled it all this way, set it in the corner if you must.
The bell still rings. You cannot hear it only because you sit too far from the bottom.
Noise is merely an uncalibrated equation. Do not crack my floor with that scrap metal of yours.
Even if you have forgotten, I will keep tolling it for you.
NEOW.talk.BELLKEEPER-BELLKEEPER.0-0.anci: ...Blind bearer of the cracked bronze... you climb once more...
NEOW.talk.BELLKEEPER-BELLKEEPER.0-1.char: The belfry collapsed. I must return the last bell to the one who cast it.
NEOW.talk.BELLKEEPER-BELLKEEPER.0-2.anci: ...The one atop the Spire... no longer remembers this bell... Will you toll it all the same...?
NEOW.talk.BELLKEEPER-BELLKEEPER.0-3.char: So long as the bronze still holds a voice, I must keep walking upward.
NEOW.talk.BELLKEEPER-BELLKEEPER.1-0r.anc: ...Listen... the heavy bronze echoes from the depths once again...
NEOW.talk.BELLKEEPER-BELLKEEPER.1-1r.cha: The stairs are not yet finished. Lend me a sliver of resonance.
NEOW.talk.BELLKEEPER-BELLKEEPER.1-2r.anc: ...Take my blessing... Let the whole Spire tremble at your peal...
DARV.talk.BELLKEEPER-BELLKEEPER.0-0.anci: Ooh! Let me see what you have strapped to your back—by the roots, an early-epoch twin-mold brass casting! Even that stress fracture is a work of art!
DARV.talk.BELLKEEPER-BELLKEEPER.0-1.char: It is not for sale. This bell belongs to the belfry; I am taking it back to the top.
DARV.talk.BELLKEEPER-BELLKEEPER.0-2.anci: To that pompous fool upstairs? He'll melt it down into gutter solder! Listen, old timer, my pack is full of priceless treasures others threw away as junk—take one, and keep that glorious chime alive!
DARV.talk.BELLKEEPER-BELLKEEPER.0-3.char: ...This dusty tome holds rubbings from the old belfry. I will take it.
DARV.talk.BELLKEEPER-BELLKEEPER.1-0r.anc: Back again, old porter! That grand brass beauty on your back sounds even richer today!
DARV.talk.BELLKEEPER-BELLKEEPER.1-1r.cha: The mountain stairs are rough; two rivets came loose on my frame. Let me feel if you have any fitting old hardware in your basket.
DARV.talk.BELLKEEPER-BELLKEEPER.1-2r.anc: Feel away! Darv never shortchanges a fellow connoisseur of antiquities!
DARV.talk.BELLKEEPER-BELLKEEPER.1-3r.cha: Old things know better than new ones how to hold onto a sound.
OROBAS.talk.BELLKEEPER-BELLKEEPER.0-0.an: The tides of the abyss and the waves of a bronze bell are born of the same ripple. Blind traveler, that little handbell at your waist yearns for a deeper resonance.
OROBAS.talk.BELLKEEPER-BELLKEEPER.0-1.ch: This is only a morning handbell used to wake the apprentices. The great bell is on my back.
OROBAS.talk.BELLKEEPER-BELLKEEPER.0-2.an: Base brass baptized by the deep may yet molt into an undying carillon; old techniques that shed their husks become the echo of midnight. Hold out your hands, and let me recast them.
OROBAS.talk.BELLKEEPER-BELLKEEPER.0-3.ch: The tone has grown heavier... as though rising from the bottom of a very deep well.
OROBAS.talk.BELLKEEPER-BELLKEEPER.1-0r.a: The scent of verdigris upon you now mingles with the brine of the tide. Are you ready to molt once more?
OROBAS.talk.BELLKEEPER-BELLKEEPER.1-1r.c: Go ahead. So long as the pitch does not stray.
OROBAS.talk.BELLKEEPER-BELLKEEPER.1-2r.a: Go forth, and let the echoes of the deep watch the steps beneath your feet.
PAEL.talk.BELLKEEPER-BELLKEEPER.0-0.anci: Slow down... why hurry so? Look at your shoulders—that broken timber frame has gouged them raw.
PAEL.talk.BELLKEEPER-BELLKEEPER.0-1.char: The bell is too heavy. If I stop and sit, my knees hurt twice as much when I stand back up.
PAEL.talk.BELLKEEPER-BELLKEEPER.0-2.anci: I know that ache... holding your breath inside your bones, enduring the crushing weight of this moment so the next moment may bloom stronger. Come, share my tears and flesh to cushion your rack.
PAEL.talk.BELLKEEPER-BELLKEEPER.0-3.char: Once this breath passes, the next step does feel lighter.
PAEL.talk.BELLKEEPER-BELLKEEPER.1-0r.anc: Still enduring in silence, old friend. Few in this Spire have the patience to wait as you do.
PAEL.talk.BELLKEEPER-BELLKEEPER.1-1r.cha: Striking a bell has always been the work of waiting for the echo. It cannot be rushed.
PAEL.talk.BELLKEEPER-BELLKEEPER.1-2r.anc: Then rest a turn... Even if you do nothing at all, time itself will stand on your side.
NONUPEIPE.talk.BELLKEEPER-BELLKEEPER.0-0: Good heavens, step off my velvet rug! Your ragged hemp robe is covered in stone dust, and that filthy rag over your eyes is a crime against fashion—wait. The patina on that bronze bell...
NONUPEIPE.talk.BELLKEEPER-BELLKEEPER.0-1: The eyeband was stained yellow by gold dust from the bell. It won't wash out. Pardon the sight.
NONUPEIPE.talk.BELLKEEPER-BELLKEEPER.0-2: Wash it out?! Are you mad?! That is authentic apex-era fire-gilding! How could such a masterpiece be strapped to a common laborer? Ugh, very well—since you escort a work of art, Madam Nonupeipe cannot let you look like a beggar. Pick an accessory!
NONUPEIPE.talk.BELLKEEPER-BELLKEEPER.0-3: I cannot see its splendor, Madam, though the fabric feels fine beneath my calluses.
NONUPEIPE.talk.BELLKEEPER-BELLKEEPER.1-0: You again, the blind beggar carrying a golden masterpiece! Did you at least polish the bell rim today?
NONUPEIPE.talk.BELLKEEPER-BELLKEEPER.1-1: Every time I toll it, the vibration shakes the dust off on its own.
NONUPEIPE.talk.BELLKEEPER-BELLKEEPER.1-2: Hmph, a rustic excuse from a rustic man. Take my gift, and do not embarrass that golden bell!
TANX.talk.BELLKEEPER-BELLKEEPER.0-0.anci: Bahahaha! Now THAT is what I'm talking about! In all my years brawling in this Spire, I've never seen a warrior strap a three-hundred-pound siege bell to his back as a bludgeon!
TANX.talk.BELLKEEPER-BELLKEEPER.0-1.char: It is not a weapon; it is a timekeeping bell. And this wooden mallet is only for striking the rim.
TANX.talk.BELLKEEPER-BELLKEEPER.0-2.anci: Don't give me that modest talk! Three floors down I heard your mallet shatter a monster's eardrums! Sound IS your warhammer! Come, grab a piece of iron from my rack and ring their skulls even louder!
TANX.talk.BELLKEEPER-BELLKEEPER.0-3.char: ...If it clears the stairs ahead, I will not refuse.
TANX.talk.BELLKEEPER-BELLKEEPER.1-0r.anc: Well met, old bell-smasher! Play me another one of those tunes that cracks stone walls!
TANX.talk.BELLKEEPER-BELLKEEPER.1-1r.cha: Stand back a step, then. Mind your ears.
TANX.talk.BELLKEEPER-BELLKEEPER.1-2r.anc: Glorious! What a kick! Take this gear and rattle every pretentious bonesack upstairs!
TEZCATARA.talk.BELLKEEPER-BELLKEEPER.0-0: Oh, you poor dear... Come sit by the hearth, old sir. Your fingers are frozen stiff, and with such dreadful bronze and broken timber weighing down your back.
TEZCATARA.talk.BELLKEEPER-BELLKEEPER.0-1: Think nothing of it, ma'am; walking keeps the blood moving. I fear if I unstrap the rack now, I may not hoist it back up.
TEZCATARA.talk.BELLKEEPER-BELLKEEPER.0-2: Even a man with a debt to deliver mustn't climb on an empty stomach and aching bones. Here—no need to unstrap the frame, just lean against the warm stones, sip some hot soup, and tuck a fresh cookie in your sleeve. The hearth will keep your old bell warm.
TEZCATARA.talk.BELLKEEPER-BELLKEEPER.0-3: ...It has been a long while since I smelled anything so warm and sweet. Thank you, kindly soul.
TEZCATARA.talk.BELLKEEPER-BELLKEEPER.1-0: I knew it was you the moment I heard the brass chime. Come warm your hands; the soup has just come to a boil.
TEZCATARA.talk.BELLKEEPER-BELLKEEPER.1-1: Following the scent of your hearth saves my blind cane half its work.
TEZCATARA.talk.BELLKEEPER-BELLKEEPER.1-2: Mind the slick steps as you go, dear. Carry this warmth inside your coat.
VAKUU.talk.BELLKEEPER-BELLKEEPER.0-0.anc: I smell the gold dust of that bastard's handiwork... Blind old ghost, you haul the Architect's bronze up these stairs—do you climb to choke the life from that arrogant creator as well?
VAKUU.talk.BELLKEEPER-BELLKEEPER.0-1.cha: No. The belfry fell, so I am returning his bell. I bear him no hatred.
VAKUU.talk.BELLKEEPER-BELLKEEPER.0-2.anc: No hatred?! He let the lower belfry crumble, blinded your eyes in the dust, left you hauling scrap like a pack mule through blood, and you are merely 'making a delivery'?! What an incomprehensible madman... Fine! So long as you march into his sanctum and ruin his peace, take my dark pacts and curses!
VAKUU.talk.BELLKEEPER-BELLKEEPER.0-3.cha: Tools have their uses, and so do curses—so long as they carry me up the final step.
VAKUU.talk.BELLKEEPER-BELLKEEPER.1-0r.an: The hollow-hearted freak returns... That chime on your back still sets my teeth on edge.
VAKUU.talk.BELLKEEPER-BELLKEEPER.1-1r.ch: If it grates on your ears, I can palm the rim until I am further up the stairs.
VAKUU.talk.BELLKEEPER-BELLKEEPER.1-2r.an: Don't bother! Save that infernal racket to shatter the Architect's ears! Take the pact and begone!
